olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A state uses 6-digit license plates where any two plates differ in at least two places. Determine the maximum number of distinct plates.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1990

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $f_1(x)=\sqrt{x^2+48}$, $f_{n+1}(x)=\sqrt{x^2+6f_n(x)}$. For each positive integer $n$, find all real solutions of $f_n(x)=2x$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1990

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Necklace $A$ has 14 beads, necklace $B$ has 19. Prove that for any odd $n\geq 1$, the 33 beads can be numbered with integers from $\{n,n+1,\ldots,n+32\}$ (each used once) so that adjacent beads are relatively prime.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1990

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find the number of positive integers whose base-$n$ representation uses distinct digits such that every digit (except the leftmost) differs by $\pm 1$ from some digit to its left.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1990

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$: circle with diameter $AB$ meets altitude $CC'$ at $M,N$; circle with diameter $AC$ meets altitude $BB'$ at $P,Q$. Prove $M,N,P,Q$ lie on a circle.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1990
